title: Activation window cohort plan and utilization buckets Q4 2026
body:
Purpose:
This is a working planning sheet for Q4 2026 activation windows. The goal: define 3 cohort waves, per-region GPU target buckets, utilization targets, and explicit activation triggers so SRE/Deploy and Capacity Ops can coordinate with Cloud vendors. This is intentionally prescriptive + conservatively biased to avoid repeat of last-minute cold-start issues.

Summary (one-liner):
Three activation cohorts (rapid, steady, reserve) across NA / EU / APAC with conservative utilization buckets (steady: 55–70%%, aggressive: 70–85%%) and explicit metric triggers to open next cohort. Timeline anchored to weekly activation windows starting 2026-10-04.

Assumptions:
- Target GPU families: H100 (large gen), A100 (fallback), L4 for low-cost embedding workloads.
- Baseline on-hosted traffic growth: 18%% month-over-month for token generation and 12%% for embeddings (from product analytics).
- Expected model mix shift toward larger context models in Q4 is accounted for via +25%% per-token compute for generation requests.
- Typical warm-up curve: first 72 hours of new wave sees 10–18%% of capacity in cold-cache inefficiency.

Activation cohorts (definition):
1) Rapid (Cohort A) — aggressive, high-confidence customers and internal traffic only. Purpose: test routing, kernel tuning, first-pass autoscaler.
   - Week 0–1: enable only on dedicated-qa pools + internal prod shadowing.
   - Target per-region initial allocation: NA: 120 H100, EU: 48 H100, APAC: 24 H100.
   - Utilization target after 7d: 50–65%% (allow burst headroom).

2) Steady (Cohort B) — customer-facing, incremental traffic shift, controlled canary.
   - Week 2–6: progressive routing of 10/25/50%% traffic slices.
   - Target per-region steady allocation: NA: 420 mixed (200 H100 / 160 A100 / 60 L4), EU: 180 mixed (80 H100 / 70 A100 / 30 L4), APAC: 120 mixed (40 H100 / 60 A100 / 20 L4).
   - Utilization target steady-state: 55–70%%; spike headroom target 85%% temporarily with autoscaler policies.

3) Reserve (Cohort C) — burst/overflow capacity and replacement for degraded AZs.
   - On-call activation only; pre-provisioned warm pool sizes kept minimal but with fast-attach capability.
   - Reserve sizes: NA: 180 (mostly A100), EU: 70, APAC: 50.

Timeline (high-level):
- 2026-10-04: Cohort A window 1 start (internal-only). Run smoke tests (routing, model fade, trace ingestion).
- 2026-10-11: Cohort A window 2 repeat for stabilization; if error budget < 0.2%% open Cohort B to 10%% traffic.
- 2026-10-25: Cohort B ramp to 25%% after two successful weeks. Verify latency p50/p95 and cost per token.
- 2026-11-15: Cohort B at 50%%; if quality regressions <= 1.5%% relative baseline, proceed to full roll to main pools by 2026-12-06.
- 2026-12-06: Target full steady-state and evaluate reserve activation plan for holiday surge (Dec 15–Jan 5).

Metric triggers (explicit):
- Open next traffic slice if all are true for 72h: p95 latency <= target, error rate <= 0.3%%, cost per 1k tokens within 10%% of forecast, inference quality metric (eval-set) delta <= 1.5%%.
- Abort/reroll if any of: p95 latency increases >20%% vs baseline for >2h, 5xx errors climb >0.5%% sustained 2h, memory OOMs observed.

Utilization bucket table (CSV rows):
Region, GPU-family, Initial-count, Steady-count, Reserve-count, Steady-util-target, Spike-headroom
NA,H100,120,200,60,60%,85%
NA,A100,0,160,120,60%,85%
NA,L4,0,60,0,40%,65%
EU,H100,48,80,20,58%,82%
EU,A100,0,70,50,58%,82%
EU,L4,0,30,0,40%,65%
APAC,H100,24,40,10,55%,80%
APAC,A100,0,60,30,55%,80%
APAC,L4,0,20,10,35%,60%

Operational notes and checklist (working):
- Pre-activation: confirm vendor batch quota and region allocation (owner: Priya). Slack ping @channel 48h before window.
- Infra: pre-pull quantized model artifacts to cache nodes 24h prior (owner: Jordan).
- Observability: add cohort tags to traces and dashboards; ensure retention for 30d (owner: Maya).
- Cost: Finance to sign off on expected incremental spend week-of (owner: Noah).
- Runbook: verify failover routes and fallback model variants are registered in rollout policy (runbook id: confluence/infra/rollouts).

Risks and mitigations (short):
- Risk: Underestimated cold-cache overhead -> Mitigation: warm-start 12% of cohort with synthetic prefix traffic 48h prior.
- Risk: Cloud vendor delay in supplying H100 -> Mitigation: stagger H100-heavy activations and provision A100 fallback lane with immediate kernel mapping.
- Risk: Spike in small embedding requests causing queue head-of-line -> Mitigation: dedicate L4 pools and rate-limit on embedding route while ramping.

Open questions / decisions needed:
- Exact SLOs for Cohort A p95 target (proposal: 180ms global p95 for generation, 80ms for embeddings).
- Confirm holiday-surge reserve budget with finance (requested: $420k incremental).
- Decide whether to enable cross-region routing for EU->NA overflow during Week 3 ramp.

Tickets and next steps (short):
- JIRA-ENGINF-1499: Create deployment pipeline for Cohort A warm pool (assigned: Jordan, due: 2026-09-28).
- JIRA-ENGINF-1502: Dashboard cohort tagging + synthetic warm traffic (assigned: Maya, due: 2026-10-02).
- JIRA-ENGINF-1511: Finance approval for reserve capacity (assigned: Noah, due: 2026-10-05).

Notes to self / loose thinking (informal):
- Consider a micro-cohort for APAC before big H100 moves; latency sensitivity is higher in certain regions (mobile gaming customers).
- If we can temporarily borrow burst capacity from partner marketplace (spot with fast attach) that reduces reserve cost by ~22%%; need SRE validation for reliability.
- Keep rollout docs minimal and include direct rollback commands for stateful caches.

Attachments / artifacts to add later:
- detailed per-AZ activation checklist (sheet)
- cost run for each cohort scenario (sheet)
- model-quant mapping table (doc)

End of working plan. Update this doc in-place as decisions come in; keep status as draft until Cohort B ramp completes.
